# dsh-delivery-board
English · 中文
> **Plan, owners, status, and handoff history in one JSON file next to your code** — no SaaS, no acc
ount; reviewed in every PR.
The board is just a view. PM and engineers trust the same `delivery.json`: stages, WIP, weekly repor
t, and an audit of moves that actually happened — so management and delivery work off one shared con
text, versioned with the repo.
*~22s silent walkthrough of the live board (v0.3.0 UI · English overlays · synthetic data). MP4 if y
ou prefer download over the inline GIF.*

## Why it exists
From Plan through requirements, design, build, test, and go-live, if delivery state is not alongside
the code, people and agents struggle to stay aligned: who owns what, what “done” means, and where w
ork is stuck often live only in handoffs and verbal sync.
**dsh-delivery-board** writes the stage pipeline, handoff trail, and client weekly report into in-re
po delivery state (`delivery.json` by default). The kanban board, calendar Timeline, audit log, and
weekly Markdown report are projections of that same state — not a separate SaaS. PMs, engineers, QA,
and AI agents share one Source of Truth that travels with the repo.
## Compared to alternatives
| Need | This project | Typical SaaS kanban | Markdown checklists alone |
| Lives in the git repo | Yes (`delivery.json`) | Usually a remote workspace | Yes, but no structure

d handoffs / WIP |
| Handoff audit + weekly client report | Built-in | Needs custom fields / exports

| Manual |
| Local editable UI + Timeline | Loopback board | Full web app | No |
| Works with AI co

ding agents | DSH skill + tools; CLI for any agent/shell | Often via API / MCP | Prompt-only |
| Sco
pe | Delivery context for one repo | Org-wide PM suite | Lightweight notes |
It is intentionally **not** a rebuild of Jira, Linear, or Notion — those are excellent for org-scale
planning. This keeps only the delivery context the current repository actually needs, offline-frien
dly and reviewable in PRs.
If this saves your team a standup or a messy weekly paste, a ⭐ star helps others find it — thank you
f this saves your team a standup or a messy weekly paste, a ⭐ star helps others find it — thank you.
## Design principles
- **Delivery state is a first-class citizen** — stages, owners, acceptance criteria (AC), Definition

of Done (DoD), handoffs, and blockers live in the repo and evolve with Git.
[该节后续省略]
## What you get
- **Stage pipeline + cards** — each card has an owner, optional description, optional `start`/`due`
dates, acceptance criteria and a checkable Definition of Done (DoD) checklist. Stages can be added,

renamed or removed after init (removing refuses while cards remain unless you migrate them).
- **Han
doff audit trail** — moving a card to another stage records who handed what to whom, automatically.
- **Weekly report** — a Markdown client report: pipeline snapshot, **shipped this week** (arrived at
the terminal stage or archived), handoffs, open risks, and **risks resolved this week**. Optional `

next_week` notes appear as **Next bets** (omitted when empty).
- **Soft WIP limits** — optional per-
stage `wipLimit` (Kanban-style). The board and move responses warn when a stage is over; moves are n

ever blocked.
- **Local editable board** — ask `/delivery Open the editable board`; the tool serves
a mouse drag-and-drop board on `127.0.0.1` that saves back to the same delivery state. Archive/resto
re, risk/blocker logging, and per-card DoD checklists are available on the board. Accessibility fall

back: Edit → Stage. Board chrome follows the browser locale (zh-CN when appropriate).
- **Timeline v
iew** — a calendar-axis Gantt of every card: bars follow real dates (created → each stage handoff →
shipped / archived / today). When both `start` and `due` are set, a schedule bar spans start→due; du
e-only cards keep the ◆ marker. Same search and owner filters as the kanban; click a title to edit.

Light and dark themes follow the OS.
- **Whole-board archive** — `archive-board` snapshots the curre
nt state (cards, logs, risks) to `delivery-archive/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.json` next to `delivery.json`
, then resets an empty board with the same pipeline/template/title. Reopen an archive read-only with

`open --file …` or `html --file …`.
- **Offline HTML snapshot** — a single read-only file teammates
without DSH can open.
Card editor, archive and dark-mode views
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations
- **Standalone CLI** needs only Node ≥20 (`npx github:jerryxff26-alt/delivery-board` now; `npx dsh-d
elivery-board` after npm publish). The DSH plugin path is a developer preview: `engines.dsh >=0.2.0-
rc.2 <0.3.0`; peers `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools >=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery ~3.18.5`

(host-provided, optional). Smoke-tested on DSH 0.2.1-rc.2; previously verified on 0.2.0-rc.2.
- No
full Gantt resource loading, hard move-blocking DoD/WIP, or realtime multi-user sync. Whole-board ar

chive is a deliberate snapshot+reset, not automatic bulk archive.
- Drag/drop (and Edit → Stage fall

back) are checked in a local browser harness; no full keyboard/mobile/WCAG claim.
- DoD checklists a
nd WIP limits are soft signals only; moving a card does not require DoD items to be checked or WIP t

o be under limit.
- Empty columns and uninitialized projects point at **one** next step (`init` / `d
elivery_init` / `/delivery …`, or **New card** on the board).
